prompt.brief: Design Design a ride-sharing platform like Uber or Lyft that matches drivers with passengers in real-time. so users can Match drivers with passengers reliably at scale.
successSignals: Define the source of truth for Match drivers with passengers; Real-time location tracking and make retries idempotent.
Use bounded, partitioned state to meet Handle 10M daily rides and Matching should happen within seconds.
Separate the critical request path from Geospatial indexing for location queries, WebSockets for real-time updates, Machine learning for demand prediction.
Explain consistency, failure recovery, authorization, observability, and a degraded mode.

functional: Support the core workflow to Match drivers with passengers.
Expose status, results, and freshness appropriate to Design a ride-sharing platform like Uber or Lyft that matches drivers with passengers in real-time..
Support authorization, validation, updates, deletion, and recovery semantics.
nonFunctional: Meet Matching should happen within seconds under normal load.
Scale to Handle 10M daily rides without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

dataFlow.title: Accept and commit the interaction
dataFlow.description: The ride sharing service gateway authenticates the actor, validates room or object membership, applies rate limits, and conditionally commits the interaction.

dataFlow.title: Publish an ordered event
dataFlow.description: An outbox emits the committed ride sharing service transition with an event ID, partition key, sequence, and replay retention.

dataFlow.title: Fan out by partition
dataFlow.description: Consumers route ride sharing service events to connected recipients, durable inboxes, or notification channels without making the origin write wait for every recipient.

dataFlow.title: Resume and reconcile connections
dataFlow.description: Clients reconnect with a cursor; the ride sharing service service replays missed events, deduplicates delivery, and exposes stale or degraded state.

dataFlow.title: Measure latency and recover
dataFlow.description: Operations tracks ride sharing service publish-to-deliver latency, hot partitions, reconnect storms, dropped events, and consumer lag for replay or repair.

architecture.title: Ride Sharing Service realtime architecture
architecture.summary: Design Design a ride-sharing platform like Uber or Lyft that matches drivers with passengers in real-time. so users can Match drivers with passengers reliably at scale. The design commits the canonical interaction before publishing a replayable event, separates hot-key fanout and aggregate projections from the write path, and treats live delivery as recoverable through versioned resynchronization.

layers.label: Interactive client and edge plane
layers.description: Commands, reads, and live subscriptions share authentication and quotas but have separate latency budgets.

layers.label: Canonical interaction plane
layers.description: Versioned durable state and committed events provide the correctness boundary.

layers.label: Fanout and live serving plane
layers.description: Workers build projections and scoped live deltas while clients can recover missed updates.

layers.label: Analytics plane
layers.description: Engagement and abuse analytics are asynchronous and isolated from feature correctness.

layers.label: Realtime safety operations
layers.description: Backlog, hot keys, connection saturation, and update loss are visible and actionable.

keyPaths.label: Interaction commit path
keyPaths.description: Client -> edge -> write service -> canonical store -> committed event.

keyPaths.label: Live update and recovery path
keyPaths.description: Event -> fanout -> read projection and live gateway -> client, with cursor-based resync.

components.label: Interactive clients
components.description: Users connect from web, mobile, or device clients and receive durable state plus live updates for the feature.

properties.protocol: HTTPS for commands; WebSocket/SSE for updates

components.label: Realtime edge gateway
components.description: Terminates connections, authenticates sessions, applies quotas, and routes commands and subscriptions to the correct partition.

properties.protection: Session auth, connection limits, and backpressure

components.label: Interaction and write service
components.description: Validates feature-specific commands, applies authorization and idempotency, and commits the canonical interaction state.

properties.consistency: Conditional writes and monotonic entity versions

components.label: Canonical interaction store
components.description: Stores users, objects, memberships, interaction state, and tombstones using the partition key needed for the hot path.

components.label: Interaction event backbone
components.description: Publishes committed interaction, membership, deletion, and moderation events with ordering keys and replay offsets.

properties.delivery: At least once with event IDs and deduplication

components.label: Fanout and aggregation workers
components.description: Updates counters, feeds, membership projections, and notification intents asynchronously with hot-key isolation and coalescing.

components.label: Low-latency read projection
components.description: Serves the latest acceptable aggregate or feed view with a version and freshness marker while preserving a durable fallback.

components.label: Live update gateway
components.description: Maintains subscription membership, coalesces rapid changes, and broadcasts scoped deltas while clients can resync from the read projection.

properties.delivery: Reconnect, cursor, coalescing, and resync support

components.label: Interaction analytics
components.description: Consumes privacy-scoped events for engagement, abuse, and product metrics without making analytics part of correctness.

components.label: Realtime reliability operations
components.description: Tracks commit latency, hot partitions, consumer lag, fanout backlog, connection health, dropped updates, resync rate, and privacy failures.

properties.alerts: Lag, hot keys, stale projections, and connection saturation

connections.label: Command or live subscription
connections.description: Clients send idempotent interaction commands and open authenticated subscriptions with a resume cursor.

connections.label: Validated interaction
connections.description: The edge validates identity, object scope, payload size, and rate limits before routing by object or conversation key.

connections.label: Canonical state commit
connections.description: The write service conditionally commits the interaction and version before returning success; duplicate retries return the existing result.

connections.label: Committed interaction event
connections.description: An outbox publishes the durable transition with an event ID, entity version, and privacy classification.

connections.label: Projection and fanout work
connections.description: Workers consume at least once, deduplicate events, isolate hot keys, and coalesce rapid updates.

connections.label: Aggregate or feed projection
connections.description: Workers update the read projection with a version and freshness watermark; rebuilds replay the event log.

connections.label: Live delta
connections.description: The live gateway receives scoped deltas, coalesces bursts, and drops only updates that clients can recover through resync.

connections.label: Read projection
connections.description: The edge serves a versioned projection and exposes a resync path when it is stale or unavailable.

connections.label: Live update
connections.description: Connected clients receive scoped updates and reconnect with a cursor when a connection or delivery gap occurs.

connections.label: Privacy-scoped analytics
connections.description: Analytics consumes a separate projection of interactions and cannot delay the canonical commit or live feature path.

connections.label: Lag and fanout telemetry
connections.description: Operations measures consumer lag, event gaps, projection freshness, hot partitions, and replay parity.

connections.label: Connection and delivery health
connections.description: The live gateway reports connection counts, send latency, coalescing, drops, reconnects, and resync rates.

deepDives.title: Ordering, idempotency, and hot keys
points: Choose a ride sharing service partition key that preserves required order while distributing high-volume rooms, users, or objects.
Use event IDs, inboxes, consumer offsets, and conditional state transitions for at-least-once delivery.
Split or isolate hot partitions without changing the client-visible sequence contract.

deepDives.title: Reconnect and replay semantics
points: Issue resumable ride sharing service cursors with an expiry and a clear snapshot-plus-delta fallback.
Bound replay windows and rebuild from durable state when a cursor is too old.
Expose version and freshness so a client can distinguish current, catching up, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Backpressure and presence
points: Keep connection heartbeats and ephemeral presence separate from durable ride sharing service interactions.
Coalesce safe updates, shed low-value work, and protect critical events during reconnect storms.
Measure end-to-end delivery, not only broker publish latency.

tradeoffs.title: Direct fan-out versus pull-based reads
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use push for latency-sensitive ride sharing service deltas and pull or replay for reconnect, history, and recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: A push-only design loses state when clients disconnect and a pull-only design wastes latency and bandwidth.

tradeoffs.title: Per-recipient queues versus shared streams
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use shared partitioned streams with per-recipient cursors where fan-out is large, and isolate exceptional high-fanout objects.
tradeoffs.caution: A queue per recipient becomes expensive and hard to inspect at large scale.

tradeoffs.title: Strong ordering versus availability
tradeoffs.recommendation: Guarantee ordering only within the scope the product needs, such as a room, object, or conversation.
tradeoffs.caution: Global ordering introduces a bottleneck and still does not solve duplicate delivery or reconnect recovery.

commonMistakes: Making every ride sharing service recipient part of the synchronous write transaction.
Assuming a websocket send means the event was durably delivered.
Using a global sequence or hot celebrity key without partition isolation.
Failing to provide cursor replay and forcing clients to reload the entire state after reconnect.
Measuring only connection count while missing delivery lag, dropped events, and reconnect storms.

followUps.question: How do you recover a disconnected ride sharing service client?
followUps.answer: Persist a bounded event stream, issue a cursor, replay missed deltas, and fall back to a versioned snapshot when the cursor has expired.

followUps.question: How do you handle a hot ride sharing service object?
followUps.answer: Separate the object’s authoritative commit from fan-out, shard or coalesce recipients, and report lag while preserving event identity.

followUps.question: Can delivery be exactly once?
followUps.answer: The network cannot guarantee it end to end; provide at-least-once delivery with idempotent event IDs, client deduplication, and replayable cursors.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the ride sharing service workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative ride sharing service state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions ride sharing service traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the ride sharing service user experience.
